subject.title: MissingAgentHarnessError race: non-atomic harness registry clear+restore during plugin cache cycle

question: What harness-preservation semantics should OpenClaw use when a gateway or plugin reload resolves to an empty plugin scope?
rationale: The code can be fixed mechanically only after maintainers choose whether empty-scope reloads preserve all harnesses, only built-in/provider-owned harnesses, or intentionally clear every plugin-owned runtime handle; that choice affects plugin disablement, security boundaries, and user-visible channel delivery.

options.title: Preserve only required provider harnesses
options.body: Keep bundled or provider-owned harnesses available across empty-scope reloads while continuing to clear disabled third-party plugin-owned harnesses.

options.title: Preserve all previous harnesses
options.body: Adopt the open repair PR's broader snapshot/restore behavior, accepting that explicit empty scopes may keep third-party harnesses live until a later full reload or restart.

options.title: Clear all and add readiness/retry
options.body: Keep fail-closed empty-scope semantics but add readiness or bounded retry behavior so channel and cron dispatch do not surface transient MissingAgentHarnessError failures.

recommendation.title: Preserve only required provider harnesses
recommendation.body: Keep bundled or provider-owned harnesses available across empty-scope reloads while continuing to clear disabled third-party plugin-owned harnesses.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has recent history in explicit plugin scope and gateway startup loader behavior, which is the central product boundary for this decision.
